page: Amazon Web Services r6gd.large is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by the custom 64-bit ARMv8 AWS Graviton2 processor using Neoverse-N1 cores running at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The instance provisions 2 dedicated physical cores matching 2 vCPUs, completely avoiding simultaneous multithreading (SMT). It is equipped with 16.0 GB of memory, providing an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside a dedicated 118 GB NVMe SSD local instance store volume and a 1 Gbps baseline network interface. Hardware cryptographic acceleration is present via dedicated AES instructions, though x86-specific vector instruction sets like AVX, AVX-512, and AMX are naturally absent.

Benchmark data reflects the entry-level compute capacity of this two-core configuration. Stress-ng single-core performance registers in the average range at 1519.49, while the aggregate multi-core score places in the bottom 25% at 3012.08. Geekbench outcomes highlight low-tier compute density with a single-core score of 944.0 and a multi-core score of 1753.0. Parallel compilation workloads using Clang score 2326.0, and synthetic PassMark tests yield a CPU score of 1349.04, reflecting lower total throughput inherent to a low core count.

Memory throughput exhibits distinct tiers depending on locality. Read bandwidth for cached small blocks reaches 117.2 GB/sec, falling into the lower decile of cloud servers, while uncached large-block reads and writes achieve 36.85 GB/sec and 18.7 GB/sec respectively. High-concurrency operations, such as Redis SET commands reaching 2.48 million operations per second, along with static web serving at 2.39 GB/sec, fall into the lower 10% benchmark tiers across all tested instances. Inference on a small 135M parameter language model demonstrates modest generation speeds at 22.18 tokens per second.

Cost efficiency is driven by the energy-efficient ARM Neoverse-N1 architecture paired with bundled high-speed local NVMe storage and a high RAM-to-CPU ratio. The trade-off centers around absolute CPU horsepower and bandwidth ceilings versus raw memory footprint and local disk speed. Workload fit includes small in-memory key-value databases, local caching tiers, read-replica relational databases, and lightweight data staging pipelines that require high memory capacity and fast scratch disk without heavy parallel compute demands.
description: Amazon Web Services r6gd.large is a memory-optimized instance featuring 2 dedicated ARM64 Neoverse-N1 cores clocked at 2.5 GHz, 16.0 GB of RAM, and a bundled 118 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume. Operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with 1 Gbps baseline networking, it offers an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio. Benchmarks emphasize moderate single-thread compute capabilities alongside low-tier multi-threaded processing, reflected in a Geekbench multi-core score of 1753.0 and stress-ng multi-core performance of 3012.08. Its memory subsystem achieves 36.85 GB/sec on uncached reads, while local caching handles Redis SET throughput at 2.48 million operations per second. The server suits memory-bound, lightweight transactional workloads, temporary scratch databases, and distributed caching tiers that leverage bundled local NVMe storage without demanding high multi-threaded compute density.
